bull_bear.body: QIP ₹183-185 cr raised Dec'25 (FDs from this inflate other income / net cash). Planning new ₹330 cr raise (QIP/rights/equivalent) by ~Sep'26 for CCL capex + working capital. Warrants ₹115 cr at ₹159 (not ₹196), 25% paid, 18-month window to ~Sep'27. Promoter holding ~47-48% post full warrant conversion, diluting to ~42-43% post ₹330 cr raise. Incentives: ~50% capex subsidy (25% central + 25% state), 15% power-cost exemption (Gujarat), logistics exemption, 7% of 9% interest exempted, 2% buyer cash subsidy on indigenous purchase.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- CCL is a brand-new line with zero firm orders — execution, quality-qualification and customer-acceptance risk; reliance on Chinese partner for tech/commissioning.
- Heavy funding dependence: ~₹650 cr need, large dilutive raise (₹330 cr) + warrants amid uncertain markets; promoter stake dropping to ~42-43%.
- Negative OCF (~-₹48 cr) and ballooning receivables (₹65→175 cr) vs only ~₹100 cr revenue growth — working-capital stress.
- Project timeline monsoon/import-dependent; no anti-dumping protection on CCL imports (competes on ~10-13% cost edge + subsidies).
- Inorganic European deal long-dated and unproven (3% net margin target).
- Macro: oil/gas, freight, metal-price inflation (mitigated by pass-through).
bull_bear.title: Risks

bull_bear.body: Highly promotional and confident, especially on CCL ("world's top line," "first-mover," "huge demand"). Heavy reliance on government-policy narrative (Modi/Vaishnaw). Finance answers vague/deferred (cash-flow and receivable questions repeatedly dodged or pushed to email/Q&A tab; numbers loosely stated, e.g. revenue/warrant figures). Audio/clarity issues throughout. Conservatism claimed on CCL margin/utilisation assumptions.
bull_bear.title: Mgmt tone

bull_bear.body:
- CCL margins (20% EBITDA / 13% PAT) far exceed core SS (~9-10%) — mix shift could re-rate consol margins if execution lands.
- After 5 lines Ratnaveer would still serve only ~2% of Indian CCL demand — market is enormous; capacity is not the constraint, quality-qualification is.
- "Net cash flow ₹203 cr" cited is gross of QIP FDs; underlying standalone OCF is negative ~₹48 cr — optics gap flagged by analyst.
- PLI/subsidy disbursed progressively per line/phase (₹35 cr on first ₹70 cr), not gated on all 5 lines — improves funding cadence.
- Warrant price corrected to ₹159 (analyst said ₹196) — info-disclosure looseness.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious

bull_bear.body:
- Fully backward-integrated manufacturing model covering scrap melting, ingot production, rolling and finished products in-house, giving operational agility, shorter lead times and consistent quality
- One of India's largest exporters of stainless-steel washers, with an extensive portfolio of 3,300+ washer SKU variants and 3,500+ fastener SKUs
- Diversified customer base of 219 customers and 89 global distribution partners across 31 countries, reducing customer concentration risk
- Upgraded credit rating from IVR BBB+ to IVR A-/Stable during the year, supporting customer, lender and partner confidence
- In-house R&D unit supporting product innovation, tooling efficiency, rapid prototyping and customisation to market-specific dimensions and finishes
- 80-90% of power consumed across the five integrated manufacturing facilities came from green energy, an advantage as global OEMs emphasise sustainable sourcing
- Breadth of internationally recognised quality certifications (ISO 9001/14001/45001, CE, PED/AD 2000, TUV and BV plant approvals) supporting export qualification
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Geographic concentration of manufacturing in a single state — All six manufacturing units — Savli/Manjusar, Waghodia and Alindra in Vadodara plus Vatva in Ahmedabad — are located in Gujarat, so a regional disruption (power, logistics, labour, regulatory or natural event) would affect the entire production base at once.
- Export dependence and cross-border trade exposure — The company describes itself as a manufacturer and exporter shipping to 31 countries across Europe, North America, Asia Pacific and the Middle East, leaving revenue exposed to overseas demand cycles, tariffs, freight and currency movement in those markets.
- Import dependence for raw material and equipment sourcing — The disclosed import sources are Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and China, so input availability and cost are tied to a small set of overseas supply origins.
- Execution and technology-partner dependence on the CCL greenfield project — The Copper Clad Laminate facility is a new vertical outside the company's established stainless-steel business, is dependent on a partnership with a leading Chinese technology company for technology transfer, installation and commissioning support, and carries a stated November 2026 commissioning date against which large topline expectations (Rs 750 crore in two years, Rs 2,500 crore in three years) have been set.
- Funding risk on planned greenfield expansion — The greenfield expansion across the electric division and the CCL business is predicated on a proposed fundraise of up to Rs 330 crore that had not been completed as at the report, following a year of repeated equity issuance via QIP, warrant and preference-share conversions.
- Product and revenue concentration in stainless steel finishing sheets — Finishing sheets alone account for 52.38% of revenue against 14.73% for washers and fasteners, 8.98% for scrap sales and 6.49% for pipes and tubes, so the earnings base leans heavily on one product line and its spread.
- Promoter concentration and related-party dependence — The Chairman & Managing Director is also the Chief Financial Officer and the largest shareholder, the board saw multiple changes during the year including the demise of the Whole-time Director, and a further executive director appointed post year-end is the Managing Director's spouse; the company has also relied on loans taken from and repaid to the Managing Director and rents premises from promoter-linked entities.
- Listing-compliance lapses attracting exchange penalties — In FY2024-25 the Company failed to give prior intimation of a board meeting for a fund-raising agenda as required under Regulation 29 of the SEBI Listing Regulations, and both stock exchanges each imposed a penalty of Rs 10,000, indicating disclosure-process weakness around capital-raising events.

business.body: Established in 2002 and headquartered in Vadodara, Gujarat, Ratnaveer Precision Engineering manufactures and exports stainless-steel products spanning washers, precision fasteners, finishing sheets, tubes and pipes, wire, solar mounting hooks and sheet metal components. outlook.body: Ratnaveer's principal expansion is the greenfield Copper Clad Laminate (CCL) project at Unit VI, Alindra (Savli, Vadodara) — announced in 2025 and described as India's first integrated FR-4 CCL manufacturing plant, with a projected capacity of 1.6 million sheets per year. Management describes FY2025-26 progress towards commissioning and states the facility will be commissioned in November 2026, with production lines progressively commissioned thereafter; the company has partnered with a leading Chinese technology company for technology transfer, installation and commissioning support. A proposed fundraise of up to Rs 330 crore is intended to support greenfield expansion across the electric division and the CCL business. The existing stainless-steel footprint comprises six units in Gujarat — SS fasteners and finishing sheets (Unit I, E 77 Savli), washers, sheet metal products and circlips (Unit II, E 78 Savli), tubes and pipes (Unit III, 120 Savli), a melting unit converting scrap to ingots (Unit IV, Waghodia) and a rolling unit converting ingots to sheets (Unit V, Vatva, Ahmedabad) — with aggregate annual processing capacity of approximately 46,668 MT. Recent capability additions include commencement of wire production and the launch of a nuts-and-bolts manufacturing vertical in FY25, which management says is now making a meaningful contribution to the fastener business.

outlook.body:
- Indian demand for stainless steel remained strong across railways, metros, construction, transportation and process industries and is expected to grow at 7-8% annually, backed by infrastructure development and rising urbanisation
- Government capital expenditure of Rs 11.21 lakh crore during the year, directed towards roads, railways, logistics, energy and urban infrastructure, creating long-term opportunities for precision engineering and stainless-steel manufacturers
- PLI 1.2 for Speciality Steel extends incentives of 4% to 15% across stainless steel flat and long products, reinforcing domestic manufacturing
- India's domestic Copper Clad Laminate market is projected to reach Rs 29,880 crore by 2031, while more than 90% of current demand is met through imports — an import-substitution opportunity
- India's electronics and PCB ecosystem is entering a phase of rapid expansion
- Growth drivers for FY26 profits were increased sales volume, cost optimization measures and expansion into new markets
- Green-energy sourcing is an increasingly important competitive advantage as global OEMs place greater emphasis on sustainable sourcing
- Credit rating upgrade from IVR BBB+ to IVR A-/Stable supports customer, lender and partner confidence

thesis: Established (2002) integrated SS washers/fasteners maker compounding ~25% on core, now making a large, government-incentivised bet to become India's first domestic copper-clad-laminate (CCL) manufacturer — substituting 100% imported PCB raw material into a market growing 30-40%, with ~50% capex subsidy and first-mover advantage.

guidance: Core SS business 25-28% CAGR → ₹1,350-1,500 cr FY27, ₹1,800 cr FY28. CCL adds ~₹750 cr at ~69% utilisation (conservative; 80-85% feasible) once all 5 lines run. Consolidated ~₹2,500 cr top line in ~2.5-3 yrs at ~13% EBITDA / ~10.5% PAT.
order book: No hard CCL pre-orders/contracts — only "soft confirmations" from PCB makers; 1-2 players reportedly willing to absorb the entire first line. Core SS order book described as "good," no demand decline seen despite war/geopolitics.
segment: Four core product lines: (a) fasteners (nut/bolt/washers + high-value spring/belly/lock washers, circlips); (b) finishing-line/bright bars; (c) sheet-metal (solar roof, auto, tailor-made); (d) tubes & pipes — backed by own melting + rolling. End-markets highly fragmented (no single customer >~10%): auto, rail/high-speed/bullet trains, marine, defence, aerospace, pharma, dairy, oil/gas, FMCG/appliances, construction/elevators. Serves 31 countries; two-star export house. NEW segment: CCL (single/double-side, TG 110-180), for semiconductors, mobiles, defence, all PCB grades.
growth: Organic: 25% core CAGR + capex ramp. New-engine: CCL (first line Nov'26 production; remaining 4 lines within ~2 yrs). Inorganic: European precision-components target (66% gross / 3% net margin there) for instant entry to Fortune-500 auto clients + cost-shifting production to India; ~10-12 months to close pending due diligence.
margins: Core SS EBITDA ~9-10.5%. CCL standalone guided ~20-21% EBITDA / ~13% PAT (mgmt calls this conservative given first-mover/import-substitution). Blended consol ~13-14% EBITDA. Input-cost inflation (oil/gas, freight, metal) being passed through to customers.
capex: CCL project ~₹351 cr + solar ₹46 cr ≈ ₹400 cr + ₹250 cr CCL working capital ≈ ₹650 cr total need. ECMS approval ₹338 cr. Capex split: ~70% plant & machinery (turnkey, Chinese), building, ~12% misc; land already owned. Timeline: machines ship from China ~Jul, install Aug-Oct, trial Oct-Nov, first production Nov'26 (monsoon-dependent, ±1-2 months). Core-business capex (FY26 ~₹115 cr) largely complete. First phase ~₹70 cr.
capital allocation: QIP ₹183-185 cr raised Dec'25 (FDs from this inflate other income / net cash). Planning new ₹330 cr raise (QIP/rights/equivalent) by ~Sep'26 for CCL capex + working capital. Warrants ₹115 cr at ₹159 (not ₹196), 25% paid, 18-month window to ~Sep'27. Promoter holding ~47-48% post full warrant conversion, diluting to ~42-43% post ₹330 cr raise. Incentives: ~50% capex subsidy (25% central + 25% state), 15% power-cost exemption (Gujarat), logistics exemption, 7% of 9% interest exempted, 2% buyer cash subsidy on indigenous purchase.
risks:
- CCL is a brand-new line with zero firm orders — execution, quality-qualification and customer-acceptance risk; reliance on Chinese partner for tech/commissioning.
- Heavy funding dependence: ~₹650 cr need, large dilutive raise (₹330 cr) + warrants amid uncertain markets; promoter stake dropping to ~42-43%.
- Negative OCF (~-₹48 cr) and ballooning receivables (₹65→175 cr) vs only ~₹100 cr revenue growth — working-capital stress.
- Project timeline monsoon/import-dependent; no anti-dumping protection on CCL imports (competes on ~10-13% cost edge + subsidies).
- Inorganic European deal long-dated and unproven (3% net margin target).
- Macro: oil/gas, freight, metal-price inflation (mitigated by pass-through).
mgmt tone: Highly promotional and confident, especially on CCL ("world's top line," "first-mover," "huge demand"). Heavy reliance on government-policy narrative (Modi/Vaishnaw). Finance answers vague/deferred (cash-flow and receivable questions repeatedly dodged or pushed to email/Q&A tab; numbers loosely stated, e.g. revenue/warrant figures). Audio/clarity issues throughout. Conservatism claimed on CCL margin/utilisation assumptions.
non-obvious:
- CCL margins (20% EBITDA / 13% PAT) far exceed core SS (~9-10%) — mix shift could re-rate consol margins if execution lands.
- After 5 lines Ratnaveer would still serve only ~2% of Indian CCL demand — market is enormous; capacity is not the constraint, quality-qualification is.
- "Net cash flow ₹203 cr" cited is gross of QIP FDs; underlying standalone OCF is negative ~₹48 cr — optics gap flagged by analyst.
- PLI/subsidy disbursed progressively per line/phase (₹35 cr on first ₹70 cr), not gated on all 5 lines — improves funding cadence.
- Warrant price corrected to ₹159 (analyst said ₹196) — info-disclosure looseness.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Vadodara-based, fully backward-integrated stainless-steel manufacturer and exporter, recognised as one of India's largest exporters of stainless-steel washers, serving customers across 31 countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Established in 2002 and headquartered in Vadodara, Gujarat, Ratnaveer Precision Engineering manufactures and exports stainless-steel products spanning washers, precision fasteners, finishing sheets, tubes and pipes, wire, solar mounting hooks and sheet metal components. Its integrated model covers the chain from stainless-steel scrap melting into ingots, rolling of ingots into sheets and finishing into export-ready products across six manufacturing units in Gujarat. Customers include global OEMs, distributors and stockists, served through a network of distribution partners across Europe, North America, Asia Pacific and the Middle East, alongside a domestic presence in twelve Indian cities.

guidance.title: Guidance

growth_optionality.title: Growth
growth_optionality.body: Organic: 25% core CAGR + capex ramp. New-engine: CCL (first line Nov'26 production; remaining 4 lines within ~2 yrs). Inorganic: European precision-components target (66% gross / 3% net margin there) for instant entry to Fortune-500 auto clients + cost-shifting production to India; ~10-12 months to close pending due diligence.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian demand for stainless steel remained strong across railways, metros, construction, transportation and process industries and is expected to grow at 7-8% annually, backed by infrastructure development and rising urbanisation
- Government capital expenditure of Rs 11.21 lakh crore during the year, directed towards roads, railways, logistics, energy and urban infrastructure, creating long-term opportunities for precision engineering and stainless-steel manufacturers
- PLI 1.2 for Speciality Steel extends incentives of 4% to 15% across stainless steel flat and long products, reinforcing domestic manufacturing
- India's domestic Copper Clad Laminate market is projected to reach Rs 29,880 crore by 2031, while more than 90% of current demand is met through imports — an import-substitution opportunity
- India's electronics and PCB ecosystem is entering a phase of rapid expansion
- Growth drivers for FY26 profits were increased sales volume, cost optimization measures and expansion into new markets
- Green-energy sourcing is an increasingly important competitive advantage as global OEMs place greater emphasis on sustainable sourcing
- Credit rating upgrade from IVR BBB+ to IVR A-/Stable supports customer, lender and partner confidence

margins.title: Margins
margins.body: Core SS EBITDA ~9-10.5%. CCL standalone guided ~20-21% EBITDA / ~13% PAT (mgmt calls this conservative given first-mover/import-substitution). Blended consol ~13-14% EBITDA. Input-cost inflation (oil/gas, freight, metal) being passed through to customers.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: QIP ₹183-185 cr raised Dec'25 (FDs from this inflate other income / net cash). Planning new ₹330 cr raise (QIP/rights/equivalent) by ~Sep'26 for CCL capex + working capital. Warrants ₹115 cr at ₹159 (not ₹196), 25% paid, 18-month window to ~Sep'27. Promoter holding ~47-48% post full warrant conversion, diluting to ~42-43% post ₹330 cr raise. Incentives: ~50% capex subsidy (25% central + 25% state), 15% power-cost exemption (Gujarat), logistics exemption, 7% of 9% interest exempted, 2% buyer cash subsidy on indigenous purchase.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Ratnaveer's principal expansion is the greenfield Copper Clad Laminate (CCL) project at Unit VI, Alindra (Savli, Vadodara) — announced in 2025 and described as India's first integrated FR-4 CCL manufacturing plant, with a projected capacity of 1.6 million sheets per year. Management describes FY2025-26 progress towards commissioning and states the facility will be commissioned in November 2026, with production lines progressively commissioned thereafter; the company has partnered with a leading Chinese technology company for technology transfer, installation and commissioning support. A proposed fundraise of up to Rs 330 crore is intended to support greenfield expansion across the electric division and the CCL business. The existing stainless-steel footprint comprises six units in Gujarat — SS fasteners and finishing sheets (Unit I, E 77 Savli), washers, sheet metal products and circlips (Unit II, E 78 Savli), tubes and pipes (Unit III, 120 Savli), a melting unit converting scrap to ingots (Unit IV, Waghodia) and a rolling unit converting ingots to sheets (Unit V, Vatva, Ahmedabad) — with aggregate annual processing capacity of approximately 46,668 MT. Recent capability additions include commencement of wire production and the launch of a nuts-and-bolts manufacturing vertical in FY25, which management says is now making a meaningful contribution to the fastener business.

management_tone.title: Mgmt tone
management_tone.body: Highly promotional and confident, especially on CCL ("world's top line," "first-mover," "huge demand"). Heavy reliance on government-policy narrative (Modi/Vaishnaw). Finance answers vague/deferred (cash-flow and receivable questions repeatedly dodged or pushed to email/Q&A tab; numbers loosely stated, e.g. revenue/warrant figures). Audio/clarity issues throughout. Conservatism claimed on CCL margin/utilisation assumptions.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Fully backward-integrated manufacturing model covering scrap melting, ingot production, rolling and finished products in-house, giving operational agility, shorter lead times and consistent quality
- One of India's largest exporters of stainless-steel washers, with an extensive portfolio of 3,300+ washer SKU variants and 3,500+ fastener SKUs
- Diversified customer base of 219 customers and 89 global distribution partners across 31 countries, reducing customer concentration risk
- Upgraded credit rating from IVR BBB+ to IVR A-/Stable during the year, supporting customer, lender and partner confidence
- In-house R&D unit supporting product innovation, tooling efficiency, rapid prototyping and customisation to market-specific dimensions and finishes
- 80-90% of power consumed across the five integrated manufacturing facilities came from green energy, an advantage as global OEMs emphasise sustainable sourcing
- Breadth of internationally recognised quality certifications (ISO 9001/14001/45001, CE, PED/AD 2000, TUV and BV plant approvals) supporting export qualification

risks.title: Risks
risks.body:
- CCL is a brand-new line with zero firm orders — execution, quality-qualification and customer-acceptance risk; reliance on Chinese partner for tech/commissioning.
- Heavy funding dependence: ~₹650 cr need, large dilutive raise (₹330 cr) + warrants amid uncertain markets; promoter stake dropping to ~42-43%.
- Negative OCF (~-₹48 cr) and ballooning receivables (₹65→175 cr) vs only ~₹100 cr revenue growth — working-capital stress.
- Project timeline monsoon/import-dependent; no anti-dumping protection on CCL imports (competes on ~10-13% cost edge + subsidies).
- Inorganic European deal long-dated and unproven (3% net margin target).
- Macro: oil/gas, freight, metal-price inflation (mitigated by pass-through).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- CCL margins (20% EBITDA / 13% PAT) far exceed core SS (~9-10%) — mix shift could re-rate consol margins if execution lands.
- After 5 lines Ratnaveer would still serve only ~2% of Indian CCL demand — market is enormous; capacity is not the constraint, quality-qualification is.
- "Net cash flow ₹203 cr" cited is gross of QIP FDs; underlying standalone OCF is negative ~₹48 cr — optics gap flagged by analyst.
- PLI/subsidy disbursed progressively per line/phase (₹35 cr on first ₹70 cr), not gated on all 5 lines — improves funding cadence.
- Warrant price corrected to ₹159 (analyst said ₹196) — info-disclosure looseness.

strategy.body:

- Partner with a leading Chinese technology company for CCL technology transfer, installation and commissioning support

- Expand the portfolio of value-added products and deliver consistent earnings quality
